scope: Existing text passkey selection, fixed two-app UI and host review, and legacy wire compatibility

checks.command: node --test tests/self-service-ui.mjs tests/self-service-text-ui.mjs tests/self-service-apps-ui.mjs tests/self-service-apps-host.mjs tests/self-service-text-host.mjs
node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit --strict --target ES2022 --module ESNext --moduleResolution bundler --lib ES2022,DOM,ESNext.Disposable tests/text-types.mts

compatibility.comparison: Direct byte equality against the clean public source archive; each source slice independently hashed with SHA-256

comparisons.covers: Configuration validation, fixed PRF salt, canonical encoding, key derivation and credential discovery

comparisons.slice: function takeCredential through end of file
comparisons.covers: Handle consumption, encryption, authenticated record format, immutable write, independent verification and recovery

comparisons.slice: Configuration and input through immediately before Operation lifecycle
comparisons.covers: Configuration and text boundaries, PRF/HKDF derivation and encrypted wire record specification

compatibility.conclusion: Text v1 stored bytes, configuration binding, PRF/HKDF rules and prepare/recover implementation are unchanged. Existing credential selection is an additive acquisition API; browser acquisition and early failure handling changed. Legacy Work and account core modules remain byte-identical.

covered: One credential creation protects two distinct app namespaces; each snapshot independently reasserts, rereads and verifies before readiness.
Same-app overwrite, swapped records, wrong credential, forged metadata handle, consumed/expired/aborted selection and implicit creation fallback are rejected.
Original-app handoff contains no credential, PRF or derived key material; forged early failure messages cannot cancel another operation.
Only the fixed textarea and markdown routes, origins and app IDs are accepted; the original shared capacity, admission limits and expiry remain enforced by host configuration.
Admission precedes the explicit native click; preparation makes one attempt; cancellation, unknown writes and late results cannot claim success or retry silently.
Recovery editor mounts only after its panel is visible and recovery succeeds; setup and late results after leaving cannot mount an editor.
Discard destroys the original editor and its undo interface; recovered text remains editable and TXT/JSON exports work after access expires.
Legacy UI fixtures inject their frozen time into existing validators; no production expiry validation was relaxed.
limitations: SDK and browser tests use controlled credential adapters; this review does not establish a physical passkey ceremony or cross-device behavior.
Apps UI tests execute actual app source with narrow DOM, SDK and editor-loader doubles; upstream editor DOM checks and browser visual checks are separate evidence.
One shared recovery client remains trusted for both cryptographically separated app namespaces.
This review performed no deployment, existing-reserve migration, production database mutation or transaction.
Automated checks are not a security audit, user-demand validation or prize-eligibility decision.
